title: Canonical URL Discovery Graph
prompt:
Implement `discover_canonical_urls(seed_url, pages) -> list[str]`. `pages` is an insertion-ordered mapping from raw absolute URL strings to iterables of raw outgoing-link strings. This is a deterministic graph-discovery exercise: no network calls occur. Canonicalize the seed, every page key, and every outgoing link. Ignore non-HTTP(S) links. Merge links from page keys that canonicalize to the same URL in page-mapping order. Discover pages breadth-first and return canonical URLs once, in first-discovery order; a discovered URL with no page mapping still appears in the result but has no outgoing links.

Canonicalization rules are: lowercase scheme and hostname; remove a default port (`80` for HTTP, `443` for HTTPS); drop the fragment; make an empty path `/`; collapse repeated `/`, `.` and `..` path segments lexically; and parse then sort query `(key, value)` pairs lexicographically, preserving blank values and duplicate pairs before URL-encoding them. Assume valid HTTP(S) URLs have no credentials or IPv6 hosts. Raise `ValueError` if `seed_url` is not absolute HTTP(S).

This deliberately has no same-host filter, async worker pool, retry policy, or raw-string queue identity. Use a queue plus a visited set over canonical URLs.

example.reasoning: The URL is normalized before graph traversal, even when it has no mapped outgoing links.
